title: Trump Says He Is Ending Limits on Methane From Drilling
summary:
President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he is ending a rule from former President Joe Biden that aimed to cut methane emissions from oil and gas drilling. He announced it in Lubbock, Texas.

Methane is an invisible gas and the main part of natural gas. Scientists estimate it causes about a third of planet-warming greenhouse gas emissions, and it warms the air faster in the short term than carbon dioxide. Oil and gas operations are the largest industrial source of methane.

Trump said the change would save companies and consumers billions of dollars and unlock 210 million barrels of oil, about 10 days of U.S. petroleum use. He put the savings at $45 billion and said the Biden plan crushed small operators with rules.

Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin previewed the changes last month. He said they would end the Super Emitter Program, which required companies to investigate and repair methane releases. Environmental groups criticized the rollback. Fred Krupp, president of the Environmental Defense Fund, said it gives companies a free pass at the expense of American consumers.
why_it_matters: The air you breathe and the planet you will grow up on can be affected by gases released when oil and gas are drilled.

background_read: Methane is a gas that can trap heat in the air and warm the planet.
It can leak out when oil and gas are drilled from the ground, so rules can require companies to find and fix those leaks.
Changing such a rule can affect both energy costs and the amount of heat-trapping gas that reaches the air.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Donald Trump, Lee Zeldin, environmental groups, and Fred Krupp of the Environmental Defense Fund.
WHAT: Ending limits on methane emissions from oil and gas drilling, including the Super Emitter Program.
WHERE: Lubbock, Texas, where Trump announced the change.
WHY: Trump said the change would save money and unlock oil, while environmental groups criticized the rollback.
